questions.question: What makes recursive SNARK verification expensive when building IVC (Incrementally Verifiable Computation)?
options: The SNARK verifier contains operations like pairing checks that translate into thousands of extra R1CS constraints per recursion level.
Recursive SNARKs require a trusted setup that grows linearly with the number of steps.
Each step must re-prove all previous steps from scratch, so proof size grows quadratically.
SNARK recursion requires hashing the full witness at every step, dominating the cost.
questions.explanation: SNARK verifiers include expensive operations (pairing checks, hash-to-curve) that each translate to many R1CS constraints, making the inner verifier circuit large and expensive to prove.

questions.question: In an R1CS constraint (Az) ∘ (Bz) = Cz, what does the ∘ symbol denote?
options: Component-wise (Hadamard) multiplication of two vectors.
Matrix multiplication of Az and Bz.
The inner dot product of Az and Bz.
The tensor product of the two vectors.
questions.explanation: The ∘ (Hadamard) product multiplies corresponding entries of two vectors of the same length, producing a vector of the same length. This is the key non-linear operation in R1CS.

questions.question: A relaxed R1CS instance has u=1 and E=[0,…,0]. What does this reduce to?
options: An ordinary R1CS check: (Az) ∘ (Bz) = Cz.
A trivially satisfied instance regardless of z.
A linear system Az = Bz = Cz.
A check that z is the all-zeros vector.
questions.explanation: With u=1 and E=0 the relaxed equation (Az)∘(Bz) = u·Cz + E collapses to (Az)∘(Bz) = Cz, exactly the standard R1CS satisfiability condition.

questions.question: For the squaring gate (a·a = b) with witnesses z1=[3,9] and z2=[5,25], what is the cross term T mod 101?
options: [97]  (which equals −4 mod 101, i.e. −(3−5)²)
[15]  (the product 3·5)
[0]   (cross terms always vanish for fresh instances)

questions.question: After folding z1=[3,9] (u1=1, E1=[0]) and z2=[5,25] (u2=1, E2=[0]) with r=17 over F_101, what are z_fold, u_fold, E_fold?
options: z_fold=[88,30], u_fold=18, E_fold=[33]
z_fold=[8,34], u_fold=2, E_fold=[0]
z_fold=[15,225], u_fold=1, E_fold=[97]
z_fold=[88,30], u_fold=17, E_fold=[97]

questions.question: Why must the prover commit to T (the cross term) before the verifier derives the folding challenge r?
options: To prevent the prover from choosing T adaptively after seeing r, which could allow forging a fold that satisfies the relaxed check with an invalid witness.
To make the proof smaller by compressing T into a single field element.
To ensure T is in the correct field, since T can otherwise overflow.
To allow the verifier to recompute T independently without the witness.
questions.explanation: If r is chosen before T is fixed, the prover can pick T as a function of r to make E_fold = E1 + r·T + r²·E2 satisfy the relaxed check even when the underlying witnesses are invalid.

questions.question: What distinguishes SuperNova from the original Nova?
options: SuperNova supports non-uniform IVC: each step can use a different circuit selected by a program counter, whereas Nova uses the same circuit at every step.
SuperNova removes the need for a final SNARK by proving the folded instance directly.
SuperNova replaces the cross term with a sumcheck protocol, reducing cost to O(log n) per fold.
SuperNova extends Nova to support lookup arguments inside the folded circuit.
questions.explanation: Nova folds two instances of the *same* circuit. SuperNova generalises this so each IVC step can select a different circuit (e.g. different VM opcodes), enabling efficient non-uniform computation.

questions.question: Attack scenario: a prover reuses the same folding challenge r for every fold in a chain of 100 steps. What can go wrong?
options: The folded witnesses become linearly dependent, letting the prover construct a fake witness that satisfies the relaxed check without corresponding to any valid computation.
Nothing: r only affects the error term E, which the verifier does not check until the final SNARK.
The prover is forced to reveal the witness, breaking zero-knowledge.
The u scalar overflows the field after enough folds, causing an arithmetic error.
questions.explanation: With a fixed r, each fold applies the same linear combination. An adversary can craft a set of witnesses that are individually invalid but combine (under the fixed r weights) to a vector satisfying the accumulated relaxed check, breaking soundness.
